summary.name: The Linux Programming Interface
summary.one_liner: A book by Michael Kerrisk that serves as a comprehensive reference to the Linux and UNIX system call API, covering files, processes, signals, threads, IPC, sockets, and terminals.
use_cases: Learning Linux system programming from the ground up
Looking up Linux API details for files, processes, and signals
Studying threads, synchronization, and IPC mechanisms
Reference for socket and network programming on Linux
Understanding terminals, pseudoterminals, and job control
summary.what_it_does: The page is the publisher's listing for The Linux Programming Interface, a book described as a comprehensive reference to the Linux API for experienced system programmers and an introductory guide for newcomers. The table of contents lists 64 chapters and six appendices. Topics include file I/O, processes, memory allocation, users and groups, time, file systems, file attributes, extended attributes, ACLs, and directories and links. Later chapters cover signals, timers, process creation and termination, threads, process groups and scheduling, daemons, secure privileged programs, and capabilities. The book also covers shared libraries, pipes and FIFOs, System V and POSIX IPC, memory mappings, file locking, sockets, terminals, alternative I/O models, and pseudoterminals. The page links to a PDF table of contents and a PDF index.
notable: Covers the Linux API in depth with 64 chapters and six appendices
Aimed at both experienced system programmers and newcomers
Includes a PDF table of contents and PDF index on the publisher page
caveats: Page text does not state a price or purchase format
Covers the Linux API only as described on the listing; no further details of edition or version are given
